newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Nine killed in latest Somalia fighting.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in latest Somalia fighting.

text.p: Nine people were killed and six wounded when fighting erupted in a north Somali village between militiamen loyal to faction leader Hussein Aideed and an ally of his rival, Ali Mahdi Mohamed, residents said on Saturday.

The residents of Dhabbad village, 600 km (360 miles) north of Mogadishu, said the fighting broke out on Friday when some villagers, supporters of Ali Mahdi's ally General Omar Haji, turned down a request to back an Aideed government.
The residents were reached by radio from Mogadishu.
Only Aideed's supporters recognise his government. Ali Mahdi is also regarded by his supporters as Somali president.

Somalia has had no government since 1991, when Hussein Aideed's father, Mohamed Farah Aideed, and other clan leaders combined to topple dictator Mohamed Siad Barre. The victors, especially the followers of Farah Aideed and Ali Mahdi, then turned on each other in a clan-based scramble for power.
Farah Aideed died in August and his supporters made Hussein Aideed, a former U.S. marine, president. Hussein Aideed has had little luck in winning popular support among the Somalis.
